title: The Torn Page
moral: Before blaming others, we should check the truth. Saying sorry can repair more than a torn page.

pages.text:
Ina loved the reading corner in her classroom.

It had soft mats, a small shelf, and a basket of books with bright covers. Her favourite book was about a little boat that crossed a big river.

One afternoon, Miss Lata allowed free reading time.

Ina reached for the boat book, but Rohan picked it first.

"I was going to read that," Ina said.

Rohan looked at the cover. "I have never read it."

Ina frowned but sat with another book.

After a few minutes, she heard a small ripping sound.

Rohan froze.

A page had torn near the bottom.

Ina stood up quickly. "You tore my favourite book!"

Rohan's eyes grew wide. "It was already loose. I only turned the page."

Ina did not believe him.

Miss Lata came over and took the book gently.

"We will repair it," she said.

Ina sat away from Rohan for the rest of the period.

Later, during packing time, Ina opened her own bag and found something strange.

A small piece of paper from the same book was inside her folder.

She remembered now.

Last week, she had borrowed the book. The loose page had caught in her folder when the bell rang. She had pulled it out quickly and forgotten about it.

Her cheeks became hot.

Rohan had not ruined the page.

She had made it weaker first.

Ina walked to him slowly.

"I am sorry," she said. "The page was loose because of me. I blamed you."

Rohan looked at her, then at the paper piece.

"So I am not a book criminal?" he asked.

Ina smiled. "No."

"Good," he said. "I was worried."

They both took the book to Miss Lata. She helped them tape the page carefully.

The tape line showed, but the little boat could still cross the river.

The next day, Ina gave the book to Rohan first.

"You finish it," she said.

Together they turned each page slowly. When the little boat reached the other side, Ina felt happy too.

The book was repaired. And so was something between them.
